claims.title: Compaction preserves rows
claims.statement: In the bounded single-source-file fixture, compaction preserves the multiset of all twelve rows at every committed snapshot and the final table across split and unsplit scan tasks, atomic and partial-progress commits, and planner residual filters.
assumptions: The fixture contains twelve rows in one source file, with no logical deletes or concurrent writers.
The formal specification assumes whole-file ownership, replacement output that copies the selected row multiset, and atomic catalog publication. It is not a proof of the Go implementation.

review.overview: Compaction may replace a physical data file only while preserving its row multiset.
scope_limits: The replay is limited to one twelve-row source file without logical deletes or concurrent writers.
The native matrix covers split and unsplit scan tasks, atomic and partial-progress commits, and planner residual filters present and absent; it checks every committed prefix and the final table.
verification_limits: Z3 and Lean check the same bounded multiplicity specification, not the Go source. Native observations determine whether each implementation preserves rows.
